root_motivation: bpolicy is the only one of the eight local agent-safety tools without a source-controlled home, tests, or a reproducible build. Every other tool tier (memlog, provfs, agentns) has a ~/wintermute/<slug>/ repo. The two follow-on PRDs (warden-policy, warden-deadman) cannot land because there is no tested, versioned base to extend. This PRD creates that home — same CLI surface, same JSON output, new Rust binary, harness — so the rest of the warden fleet has something to test against and diff.
user_persona: jsy — running this laptop's agent-safety stack. Uses bpolicy to enforce write restrictions on Claude agent PIDs. Consumes bpolicy status JSON in drift skill and CLAUDE_SELF.md. Expects back-compat with the existing Python CLI surface byte-for-byte.

acceptance_criteria.description: bpolicy --help lists exactly six subcommands: load, unload, enforce, release, status, log. A test asserts each appears.
bpolicy status with no BPF loaded prints exactly {"loaded": false} (the same as Python). A golden test compares against the Python reference output.
When loaded (mocked: fixture faking bpftool -j map dump output), status produces the documented shape with protected_pids sorted ascending and stats keyed checked/allowed/denied/forked_in.
enforce/release translate a PID to the same little-endian u32 key bytes the Python pid_to_key_bytes produces. Unit test asserts for PID 0, 1, 65535, 4194304.
load and unload are idempotent: second load prints {"already_loaded": true}; second unload prints {"already_unloaded": true}. Tested against a mock pin-exists check.
reference/bpolicy.py is present and README documents the behavioral contract and the BPOLICY_OBJ override.
cargo clippy -D warnings and cargo test are green (MSRV 1.85, no let-chains). Privileged paths (sudo -n bpftool) isolated in bpf.rs behind a trait so tests inject a mock and never invoke sudo.
bpf/build.sh compiles bpf/bpolicy.bpf.c to bpolicy.bpf.o. Deferred if no clang/bpftool in build env — declared as deferred AC.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/mocks/ac8.rs::test_build_sh_exists_and_executable (deferred: real compile skipped if clang absent)

scope: Rust CLI binary at ~/wintermute/bpolicy/ replacing the Python bpolicy script
Same six subcommands: load, unload, enforce, release, status, log
Byte-identical JSON output to the Python reference implementation
BPF source vendored into bpf/ directory unchanged from ~/.local/src/bpolicy/
Test harness with mocked bpftool subprocess so tests never invoke sudo
reference/bpolicy.py kept for diffing and documentation
non_goals: No BPF behavior change — .bpf.c vendored verbatim
No loading the enforcer as part of this PRD — home and harness only, arming is user's call
No hardcoded allow-list changes — warden-policy handles that
No deadman logic — warden-deadman handles that
No service/daemon — this is a CLI only
No automatic install replacing ~/.local/bin/bpolicy — install is manual per README

additional.no_network_in_tests: tests must never invoke sudo or bpftool; all privileged ops mocked via trait
additional.back_compat: JSON output must be byte-identical to the Python reference for status subcommand

five_whys_trace.q: Why create a Rust replacement for the Python bpolicy script?
five_whys_trace.a: The Python script has no source-controlled home, no tests, no reproducible build — it is the only one of eight agent-safety tools that cannot be diffed or regression-tested.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does it need source control and tests specifically?
five_whys_trace.a: The two follow-on PRDs (warden-policy, warden-deadman) are rust-extend into this repo. They have nowhere to land and nothing to test against until the home + harness exist.

five_whys_trace.q: Why must the JSON output be byte-identical to the Python?
five_whys_trace.a: The drift skill and CLAUDE_SELF.md already cite bpolicy status output; any shape change silently breaks a skill. This PRD makes 'same surface, new home' an explicit tested invariant.

five_whys_trace.q: Why Rust specifically rather than just version-controlling the Python?
five_whys_trace.a: The wintermute-home rule (memory feedback_wintermute_home) requires Rust CLIs built for this system to live at ~/wintermute/<slug>/. The follow-on warden-policy and warden-deadman PRDs are Rust-extend; they need a Rust base. Additionally, the other seven tools are already Rust.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should the installed binary replace ~/.local/bin/bpolicy automatically?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No. The PRD explicitly says install is manual: 'install -m755 target/release/bpolicy ~/.local/bin/bpolicy'. The README documents this step.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What is the BPOLICY_OBJ env override for?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The installed binary reads the BPF object from ~/.local/src/bpolicy/ by default (so existing pinned paths are not stranded). BPOLICY_OBJ overrides to point at the repo copy during development.
